skill.name: clojure-review
skill.description: Review Clojure and ClojureScript code changes for Metabase style, module, API, test, and quality conventions.
skill.summary: Review Metabase Clojure changes for style, organization, API, test, and module convention issues.
skill.author: metabase

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives. The backtick findings are Markdown inline code spans, the path findings are static shared-document includes, and no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: - If `CLOJURE_STYLE_GUIDE.adoc` exists in the working directory, also check compliance with the comm
- [ ] Public vars in `src` or `enterprise/backend/src` have useful docstrings
- [ ] `TODO` comments include author and date: `;; TODO (Name 2025-01-01) -- description`
- [ ] No `declare` when avoidable (public functions near end)
- [ ] No blank, non-comment lines within definition forms (except pairwise constructs in `let`/`cond
- [ ] Separate `deftest` forms for distinct test cases
- [ ] Query params use kebab-case, bodies use `snake_case`
- [ ] No raw MBQL manipulation outside `lib`, `lib-be`, or `query-processor` modules
- [ ] Uses `t2/select-one-fn` instead of selecting full rows for one column
- [ ] Passes `driver` argument to other driver methods (no hardcoded driver names)
- [ ] Kondo linter suppressions use proper format (not `#_:clj-kondo/ignore` keyword form)
| `;; TODO fix this`                           | Missing author/date: `;; TODO (Name 2025-01-01) --
| `(defn foo ...)` in namespace used elsewhere | Should be `(defn ^:private foo ...)`
| Query params with `snake_case`               | Use kebab-case for query params
> This pure function should be named as a noun describing its return value. Consider `user` instead
> This function is only used in this namespace, so it should be marked `^:private`.
> Query parameters should use kebab-case. Change `user_id` to `user-id`.
- Do not post comments confirming things "look good" or telling them they did something correctly

content.value_statement: Clojure pull request reviews can miss Metabase style rules and module conventions. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to find concrete review comments.
actual_capabilities: Reviews Clojure and ClojureScript diffs against Metabase coding standards.
Checks naming, documentation, privacy markers, line length, and function organization.
Flags REST API, module, MBQL, database, driver, and test convention issues.
Limits review comments to style violations and potential quality problems.
Provides concise examples for reviewer feedback on common issues.
limitations: It is tailored to Metabase conventions, not general Clojure style alone.
It does not run tests, linters, or build commands by itself.
It needs a relevant diff or changed files to produce useful review comments.
It is not a broad security audit or performance profiling tool.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Check Clojure and ClojureScript pull requests before posting review comments.

use_cases.title: Prepare Contributions
use_cases.description: Find style and convention issues before submitting a Metabase contribution.

use_cases.title: Train Reviewers
use_cases.description: Learn the checklist used for Metabase Clojure reviews through focused feedback examples.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Diff Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small Clojure change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Clojure diff for Metabase style issues. Flag only concrete violations and explain the requested change.

prompt_templates.title: Test Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Review changes that add or update tests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Clojure test changes. Check test names, separate test cases, parallel markers, and missing coverage expectations.

prompt_templates.title: API Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Metabase API change. Check route naming, request parameter style, response schemas, side effects, and required tests.

prompt_templates.title: Full Convention Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across several Metabase areas.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this mixed Clojure and ClojureScript pull request. Prioritize module boundaries, REST API conventions, MBQL usage, database access, and driver method rules.

output_examples.input: A pull request adds a new public helper without documentation.
output_examples.output: The review identifies the missing docstring and asks for purpose, inputs, and outputs before merge.

output_examples.input: A backend change adds a plural REST route and omits endpoint tests.
output_examples.output: The review flags the route naming issue and requests tests for the new endpoint.

output_examples.input: A database change selects a full row to read one value.
output_examples.output: The review recommends selecting only the needed value and keeping data access logic in the expected layer.

best_practices: Provide the full diff and relevant surrounding files for context.
Ask for comments only on actionable violations or quality risks.
Review generated feedback before posting it to a pull request.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to praise changes that already follow the guide.
Do not treat its feedback as a replacement for tests or linters.
Do not apply Metabase-specific rules to unrelated Clojure projects without review.

faq.question: What languages does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews Clojure and ClojureScript changes, especially in the Metabase codebase.

faq.question: Does it run clj-kondo or tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and does not execute linters, tests, or build tools.

faq.question: Can it review non-Metabase projects?
faq.answer: It can help, but many checks are specific to Metabase naming, module, and API conventions.

faq.question: What kind of comments should it produce?
faq.answer: It should produce actionable comments about style violations, missing documentation, and quality concerns.

faq.question: Should it post positive review comments?
faq.answer: No. The skill directs reviewers to avoid comments that only say a change looks correct.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
